blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Prehistory denotes the vast span of human existence prior to the invention of writing and written records.
The fundamental basis for classifying the Prehistoric Age is the evolution, material, and manufacturing techniques of stone tools.
Knowledge of prehistoric human life is reconstructed exclusively through archaeological finds, including stone implements, fossils, and cave art.
The Prehistoric Age in Indian history is broadly categorized into Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, Neolithic, and Chalcolithic ages.

blocks.content: Prehistory refers to the long span of human past before the invention of writing. Since writing had not yet developed, historians cannot rely on inscriptions, manuscripts, or literary sources to understand this period. Instead, the reconstruction of prehistoric life depends entirely on archaeological evidence such as stone tools, bones, fossils, cave paintings, and habitation sites.
In competitive examinations like SSC, a very clear distinction is made: - History deals with written records. - Prehistory deals with periods where no written records exist.
This distinction is extremely important for objective-type questions.
Basis of Classification of the Prehistoric Age

The Prehistoric Age is classified mainly on the basis of the tools used by humans. As humans progressed, their tools became more refined, which also reflects changes in their lifestyle and social organisation.

items: Prehistory is defined by the complete absence of written script, relying solely on archaeological evidence for historical reconstruction.
Exam questions frequently test the classification parameters of stone tools across Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic phases.
Understand the conceptual distinction between Prehistory (no script), Proto-history (script exists but undeciphered), and History (written records available).
